column1: # boru Language Specification: fnsig — the function TYPE
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# `fnsig` builds a FunctionSignature: a structural function shape with
# no body. Two forms, mirroring `fn` exactly one slot shorter — a
# function TYPE is a function minus its body:
#   fn    input output body        a function
#   fnsig input output             its type            (§1)
#   fn    [[in] [out] [body] …]    spec-list form
#   fnsig [[in] [out] …]           spec-list form      (§2)
# The pair form's input slot carries the same `tnot List` Pattern as
# fn's triple: a LIST input always selects the spec-list form, so 2+
# parameters, zero parameters and overload sets keep the bracketed
# spelling. See design/legacy/FUNCTION-TYPES.0.ignore.
# Bound to a capitalised name, a FunctionSignature is a TYPE that
# dispatch enforces (core/go/unify_fnundef_named.go): a parameter
# declared `g:IntToStr` admits only functions whose shape satisfies it,
# where a bare `Function` parameter admits any function at all.
# §1  the pair form, and its identity with the spec-list form
typeof (fnsig Integer String)
column3: the pair form builds a FunctionSignature

column1: deq (canon (fnsig Integer String)) (canon (fnsig [[Integer] [String]]))
column3: pair form and spec-list form build the SAME value

column1: deq (canon (fnsig Integer Integer)) (canon (fnsig [[Integer] [Integer]]))
column3: …likewise when input and output coincide

column1: # The OUTPUT slot follows fn's abbreviation rule: a bare type and a
# one-element list mean the same thing, so `fnsig Integer [String]` is
# the same value as `fnsig Integer String`. (The INPUT slot cannot be
# bracketed — a list there always selects the spec-list form, §2.)
typeof (fnsig Integer [String])
column3: a bracketed OUTPUT stays in the pair form

column1: deq (canon (fnsig Integer [String])) (canon (fnsig Integer String))
column3: …and is the same value as the bare output

column1: deq (canon (fnsig Integer [String])) (canon (fnsig [[Integer] [String]]))
column3: …and as the full spec-list spelling

column1: def T fnsig Integer [String]  def f fn x:Integer String [convert String x]  def h fn g:T String [(g 5)]  h f/v
column3: …and it dispatches identically

column1: # §2  the spec-list form is undisturbed by the pair sugar
typeof (fnsig [[Integer] [String]])
column3: 1-triple spec list

column1: typeof (fnsig [[Integer Integer] [Integer]])
column3: 2-parameter input needs the spec-list form

column1: typeof (fnsig [[] [Integer]])
column3: zero-parameter shape

column1: typeof (fnsig [[Integer] [String] [String] [Integer]])
column3: an overload set is one list of pairs

column1: fnsig [[Integer]]
column3: an odd-length spec list is refused

column1: fnsig []
column3: an empty spec list is refused

column1: # §3  a named fn-shape type ADMITS a function whose shape satisfies it
def T fnsig Integer String  def f fn x:Integer String [convert String x]  def h fn g:T String [(g 5)]  h f/v
column3: the declared shape admits a matching function

column1: def T (fnsig [[Integer] [String]])  def f fn x:Integer String [convert String x]  def h fn g:T String [(g 5)]  h f/v
column3: …and the spec-list spelling of the same type behaves identically

column1: def f fn x:Integer String [convert String x]  def h fn g:(fnsig Integer String) String [(g 5)]  h f/v
column3: an ANONYMOUS fn-shape annotation needs no name

column1: def T (fnsig [[Integer Integer] [Integer]])  def f fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][add a b]]  def h fn g:T Integer [(g 2 3)]  h f/v
column3: a 2-parameter shape admits a 2-parameter function

column1: # §4  …and REFUSES one that does not. This is what a bare `Function`
#     parameter cannot do: it admits every function and defers the
#     failure to run time.
def T fnsig Integer String  def f fn x:String Integer [size x]  def h fn g:T String [(g 5)]  h f/v
column3: String->Integer does not satisfy Integer->String

column1: def T fnsig Integer String  def f fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][String][convert String a]]  def h fn g:T String [(g 5)]  h f/v
column3: arity mismatch is refused

column1: def T fnsig Integer String  def h fn g:T String [(g 5)]  h 42
column3: a non-function is refused

column1: # §5  variance — parameters contravariant, returns covariant. A
#     function that accepts MORE and returns LESS is substitutable;
#     the reverse is not.
def T fnsig Integer Number  def f fn x:Number Integer [1]  def h fn g:T Integer [(g 5)]  h f/v
column3: Number->Integer satisfies Integer->Number

column1: def T fnsig Number Integer  def f fn x:Integer Number [1]  def h fn g:T Integer [(g 5)]  h f/v
column3: …and Integer->Number does NOT satisfy Number->Integer

column1: # §6  `is` and dispatch agree — one structural rule, two call sites
def T fnsig Integer String  def f fn x:Integer String [convert String x]  f/v is T
column3: `is` admits the same function dispatch admits

column1: def T fnsig Integer String  def f fn x:String Integer [size x]  f/v is T
column3: …and refuses the same one dispatch refuses

column1: def T fnsig Integer String  5 is T
column3: a non-function is not an inhabitant of an fn shape
